title: B.B. King, Queen Booking and Ruth Bowen
summary: Thomas regrets missing B.B. King and describes Ruth Bowen, his saxophone-studio tenant, becoming Dinah Washington's manager.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Yeah. The one guy I missed on was B.B. King. If I'd had the knowledge that I know now... See, I went to work for Queen, which wasn't aware of the booking business like Shaw was. And I...
Well, they didn't have the knowledge of getting contracts and...
Ruth Bowen was the head of it. But the...
That (?) in Washington(?)? This company was his?
Well, that's what I want to know. Tell me about it.

Well, I was a good friend... See, I kind of halfway gave... I didn't give her a start, but when I had the saxophone studio, I rented out to the saxophone studio to Ruth Bowen to do publicity. I talked her into being a personal for Dinah. Because I told her, "it's a possibility that Dinah needs somebody with a little class" -- because Dinah didn't have no class. She'd cuss somebody out. I remember she played in Chicago, and the man said she did a wonderful business to the end of the week, and when she closed, she come out cussin' everybody out. She was just

like that. But Dinah liked me, and Dinah would have liked to have hired me when her agency first started. I even told Ruth how to get her agency license. I said, "Call Joe Glaser, and he'll help you get you license." Because Joe was just like that; he'd do you a favor...
